description: Antonov An-2T in German civil marks, kept in flying condition. The museum own page gives 1957 as the year of construction. Spottingmode status pre; last noted July 2025. Also listed on the museum's own collection page.

De Havilland DH.82A Tiger Moth in German civil marks, kept in flying condition. The museum own page gives 1942 as the year of construction. Spottingmode status pre; last noted July 2025. Also listed on the museum's own collection page.

North American P-51D Mustang, United States serial 44-73149, in Turkish civil marks TC-SMO and painted as B7-H Ferocious Frankie. Airworthy; a veteran of Saving Private Ryan, Memphis Belle and Fury. Acquired January 2018. Spottingmode status pre; last noted July 2025. Also listed on the museum's own collection page.

Piper PA-32 carried in the Spottingmode register without a registration and painted as TC-SVG. Tail number left blank because the true identity could not be established; the museum own collection list does not name a PA-32.

Boeing Stearman A75N1 in Turkish civil marks, kept in flying condition. The museum own page gives 1940. Spottingmode records the type as an E75; the construction number 75-863 is consistent with A75N1 production.

Boeing Stearman A75N1 in Turkish civil marks, kept in flying condition, wearing the number 196. The museum own page gives 1943. Spottingmode status pre; last noted July 2025. Also listed on the museum's own collection page.

North American T-6G Texan in United States civil marks, kept in flying condition and named Happy Hour. The museum own page gives 1953. Spottingmode status pre; last noted July 2025. Also listed on the museum's own collection page.

Cessna 195A Businessliner in United States civil marks, kept in flying condition. The museum own page gives 1950. Spottingmode status pre; last noted July 2025. Also listed on the museum's own collection page.

Fouga CM.170 Magister jet trainer in United States civil marks, held as a static exhibit. The museum own page gives 1966. Spottingmode status pre; last noted July 2025. Also listed on the museum's own collection page.

Douglas DC-3A in United States civil marks, kept in flying condition and named Turkish Delight. Delivered 1940 as Flagship Cleveland, later USAAF, Trans Texas, Provincetown-Boston and Champlain Air; completed a round-the-world flight in 2017 under Breitling sponsorship. Acquired March 2019. Spottingmode status pre; last noted July 2025. Also listed on the museum's own collection page.

Bell UH-1H Iroquois in United States civil marks, kept in flying condition. The museum own page gives 1967. Spottingmode status pre; last noted July 2025. Also listed on the museum's own collection page.

Supermarine Spitfire Mk IX built at Castle Bromwich in 1945 and issued to 33 Maintenance Unit and then to 313 Czechoslovak Squadron in Kent on 21 July 1945. Held under its wartime serial TE517; the museum own page is the source. No Turkish Spitfire survives, and the museum presents this aircraft as a stand-in for the 196 Mk IXs Turkey operated between 1947 and 1948.
aliases: Spitfire Mk IX;Spitfire;Spitfire IX;LF Mk IXe

description: Focke-Wulf Fw 190A-5 rebuilt to flying condition from the wreck of an aircraft manufactured in 1943 under Werknummer 1134 and shot down over northern France in 1944. Donated by Ali Ismet Ozturk in January 2025, arrived at Sivrihisar 8 May 2025, restored by the Mach Teknik team and flown in Turkey for the first time on 3 July 2026 wearing Turkish Air Force square markings. Tail number left blank; the airframe carries no serial, only the Werknummer.
North American T-28B Trojan, United States Navy BuNo 138354, kept in flying condition. Donated by Ali Ismet Ozturk in November 2021; the museum own page is the source.

Flying replica of the Vecihi XIV, the 1930 Vecihi Hurkus design that became the first Turkish aircraft to receive an airworthiness certificate. Built from an E75 fuselage by the Mach Teknik team for the Sivrihisar Aviation Club and the museum, first test flight June 2025, entered the museum inventory 28 June 2025. Recorded as a replica; approximately 80 per cent visual fidelity to the original. No serial is carried.

Flying replica of the Nu.D.36 trainer designed by Selahattin Resit Alan for Nuri Demirag. Built over eight months by Ali Ismet Ozturk and his technical team and added to the museum inventory at a ceremony on 29 August 2026 with a flying display. Recorded as a replica; no serial is carried.
Pietenpol Air Camper homebuilt, held as a static exhibit. Listed on the museum own static inventory page; no registration or construction number is published, so the tail number is left blank.
Boeing Stearman E75 (PT-13D) fuselage only, held as a static exhibit and donated by Ali Ismet Ozturk. The museum own page gives 1942. No registration is published, so the tail number is left blank.
Aerolite 103 single-seat ultralight, held as a static exhibit. The museum own page gives 1997. No registration is published.
Phantom X2 two-seat ultralight restored at the Sivrihisar Aviation Centre and donated by Mustafa Yavuz. The museum own page gives 1986. No registration is published.
Polaris Skin 582 two-seat microlight built in Italy, kept in flying condition and donated by Mustafa Yavuz in April 2019. The museum own page gives 2008. No registration is published.
